real_defects.issue: Out-of-range clock times were accepted: a time column of 77:30 put the reading three days later (span 3.2 days, coverage 1.3%), and a timestamp of 14:75 or 24:30 was rolled into a later hour. mk and parseTimeOfDay now refuse minutes over 59 and hours past 24:00, so the line is skipped and counted.

finish() took the UPPER median of the gaps between readings as the interval, so a short paste of 15-minute data with one missing line (gaps 15, 30) was read as 30-minute data: peak halved (2 kW instead of 4), coverage 120%, and the 'understates' warning shown. Now the lower median: a missing reading only ever lengthens a gap.
Sibling of the first: parseTimestamp's realUtc caught a day rolling over but not minutes, so 2026-03-04 14:75 and 3/4/2026 2:75 PM were read as 15:15. Now refuses hours over 23 and minutes over 59.

toMin (used by sitreport.mjs parseTimes and hhmm for medication authorisation and dose times) accepted minutes over 59 and hours over 12 with am/pm: '8:75pm' stored as 21:15, '13pm' as 01:00, so dose-spacing checks ran on a time nobody wrote. Found by the new check_clock_rollover.py on its first run. Now refused; 24:00 still means end of day.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
